value.rationale: The two-time resolution of the hidden common reset clock is a physically natural inference problem because all N particles share one age but independent thermal fluctuations obscure it. Harmonic confinement saturates conditional variance, making the maximum discriminable age grow only like (log N)/(4 κ) even when N is large, and a sharp Gaussian crossover describes the critical experimental regime. Averaging calibrated experiments over the physically dictated Poisson age law produces a nontrivial exact power exponent r/(4κ) and coefficient, not available from known stationary energy moments or extremes. This constitutes a motivated complete statistical boundary rather than an arbitrary fixed-parameter computation. Its calibration requirement and statistical-model restrictions are explicitly stated.
